title: 1.1 Meet the People
unit_outcome: Understand and produce simple sentences about people, family members, and actions.
goal: Identify a boy, girl, man, and woman, then use he or she in a short identity sentence.
grammar_function: A + singular person; He/She is a + singular person.
prerequisite: No prior English is required; this is the first course lesson.
speaking_outcome: Say four short identity phrases with a boy, girl, man, or woman.

cards.pedagogy_note: The first person arrives; a introduces one person with boy.
The same boy appears in different clothes so he refers to the person, not the shirt.
The first two anchors combine into the lesson's first complete sentence.
A second child joins the same meet-the-people sequence.
The same girl changes clothes before the learner links her to she.
The girl follows the same noun-to-pronoun-to-sentence pattern as the boy.
The story now introduces the adult male counterpart to the boy.
The fourth person completes the cast and prepares age and pronoun contrasts.
The learner first separates child from adult within the male pair.
The matching female age contrast follows naturally.
All four people now appear together as distinct visual categories.
The cast repeats with new clothing and a new answer position.
The known he-is-a frame grows from boy to man.
The matching she-is-a frame grows from girl to woman.

cards.spanish_translation: Elige la frase para el niño.
cards.pedagogy_note: Direction reverses from words-to-image to image-to-sentence.

cards.spanish_translation: Elige la frase para la mujer.
cards.pedagogy_note: Recognition ends on the adult counterpart, ready for audio-only retrieval.
Audio removes the visible target text while preserving the first age contrast.
The female age contrast immediately mirrors the previous card.
The learner now retrieves the complete male identity sentence by ear.
The complete female identity sentence follows in the same structure.
All four people return for a larger listening choice.
Listening closes with the girl who followed the boy in the opening story.
Production begins with the shortest familiar boy phrase.
The learner expands from a noun phrase to the complete girl sentence.
The same frame transfers from the child to the adult man.
The adult woman completes the four-person production set.
The boy returns in new clothes so the learner produces his complete identity independently.
The learner supplies the pronoun for the first person in the story.
The matching girl completion follows with the answer position changed.
Attention moves from the pronoun to the linking word is.
The next completion focuses on the article that introduced every person.
The lesson resolves by recognizing the same boy despite his changed clothing.
